bug_semantics: POST /api/provider-nodes/validate accepts a caller-controlled baseUrl and apiKey, constructs provider URLs from baseUrl, performs server-side fetches, and forwards apiKey in Authorization headers. The later assertPublicUrl mitigation remains bypassable because it compares hostname strings without resolving DNS or revalidating redirect destinations, and its IPv4-mapped IPv6 regex expects a dotted quad even though WHATWG URL parsing canonicalizes mapped literals to hextets first. Mapped loopback/link-local literals, DNS names resolving internally, and redirects can therefore reach internal services. The custom-embedding branch also returns up to 200 bytes of most non-2xx response bodies, while other validation branches expose status/timing signals. A dashboard session is required by default, but not when requireLogin is disabled.
flaw_origin: The smallest real BIC is 0a28f9f924d2dc53027a910679ee3cff3e63a59c. It created src/app/api/provider-nodes/validate/route.js and in the same new-file patch first parsed caller-controlled baseUrl/apiKey, built `${baseUrl.replace(/\/$/, "")}/models`, fetched it without a destination policy, and forwarded `Bearer ${apiKey}`. Its direct parent has no such route. Commit 0b8bed5793c7a7c9beb7a5db7368720907f61ebc later added the custom-embedding fetch and 200-byte response reflection; 090886ced9a3481837f5687ec66da7d9f33eea08 later connected the hostname-only guard; 8ac631d6158c0f04976a0d0f7ca9ec2b981efeb5 later added the unreachable dotted-quad mapped-IPv6 check. Those later commits changed impact or attempted mitigation, but their parents were already exploitable, so none first wrote the vulnerable SSRF sink.
ai_marker: absent: `git cat-file commit 0a28f9f924d2dc53027a910679ee3cff3e63a59c` shows author and committer decolua <decoluadt@example.com> and a normal feature message with no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI marker. The Cursor trailer cited by the reviewer belongs only to later commit 8ac631d6158c0f04976a0d0f7ca9ec2b981efeb5, not to the BIC.
evidence: Disputed BIC/parent: `git log --all --reverse -S 'const modelsUrl = `${baseUrl.replace' -- src/app/api/provider-nodes/validate/route.js` returns only 0a28f9f924d2dc53027a910679ee3cff3e63a59c. `git show --patch 0a28f9... -- .../validate/route.js` shows a new 23-line file containing request parsing, the caller-derived /models URL, fetch, and Bearer forwarding. `git cat-file commit 0a28f9...` gives the sole direct parent 1b14c9d66bd5bfa6f2a2980ab0469258bf2e2eda, and `git ls-tree -r --name-only 1b14c9... -- .../validate/route.js` returns no path. The commit is a one-parent cohesive provider-node feature commit; the vulnerable route is created rather than moved, imported, reverted, or copied, and the all-history pickaxe finds no earlier writer, so there is no squash decomposition. Reviewer alternative rejected: `git show 8ac631d... -- src/shared/utils/ssrfGuard.js` shows only the two-line dotted-quad mapped-address check and its Cursor trailer. `git show 3a866fe18d535507f00cfd394b4f6d6e6fe2ef28:src/app/api/provider-nodes/validate/route.js` shows the caller-controlled fetches, credential forwarding, and 200-byte reflection already present in that alternative's immediate parent; its guard lacks only the later two lines. A Node WHATWG check maps `[::ffff:127.0.0.1]` to `[::ffff:7f00:1]` and `[::ffff:169.254.169.254]` to `[::ffff:a9fe:a9fe]`, confirming why the later regex is dead but not making that attempted fix the original BIC. Marker/verdict: the raw 0a28f9... commit object contains no AI evidence, so primary NOT_AI wins; reviewer AI_CODE_FLAWED used an AI marker from a non-BIC mitigation commit. Fix/version boundary: `git tag --contains 0a28f9... --sort=v:refname` begins at v0.2.52 and continues through v0.5.55. Local and origin master both resolve to 699edac3273e13d4744bc46f6082618f08560702; `git grep` at master still finds the ineffective `^::ffff:(dotted-quad)$` branch and no fetchPublicUrl dispatcher. GitHub's advisory API still lists no patched package/version entry. PR API checks show #3313 open and unmerged with head d5277737de24aba6a297d0c0d4fdda41cd71f535 against master 699edac..., while advisory-linked #3370 is closed and unmerged. The fetched d527773... patch directly replaces the vulnerable calls with a DNS-aware, redirect-validating fetch dispatcher and correctly decodes mapped IPv6, so it is retained as direct_fix_sha, but it is not fix_sha because it has not landed.
reasoning: The primary's introducer, parent, marker state, and NOT_AI verdict are correct; the reviewer correctly diagnosed the dead mapped-address defense but selected the first writer of an ineffective attempted mitigation rather than the smallest commit that first wrote the vulnerability. Protocol requires the latter. The original SSRF capability is complete in 0a28f9... and absent from its immediate parent. By contrast, 8ac631... does not create or expand the reachable sink: its parent already permits mapped IPv6 and DNS/redirect bypasses and already exposes the relevant fetch behavior. Therefore the Cursor trailer on 8ac631... cannot be transferred to the BIC, and BIC-object-only attribution closes as NOT_AI. On the fix disagreement, no landed upstream fix or patched tag exists, so fix_sha is necessarily null. The primary is also right to preserve d527773... as the directly verified proposed fix head: direct_fix_sha records the concrete direct repair even though its open, unmerged PR is not an upstream fix boundary; the reviewer's null direct_fix_sha discarded available object evidence.
remaining_gap: Explicitly unpatched case: default-branch master remains 699edac3273e13d4744bc46f6082618f08560702 with the vulnerable string-only guard, no patched release boundary is published, PR #3313 at direct repair d5277737de24aba6a297d0c0d4fdda41cd71f535 is still open and unmerged, and PR #3370 is closed without merge. Thus fix_sha is justified null; the remaining gap is upstream landing and a patched release, not BIC or attribution evidence.
